Research notes and unresolved questions

Merged event, two phases (Boole 1847, Stone 1934-37), not competing priorities. Derived methodological is 1847 for Boole’s use of algebra on logic; Stone’s separate application to topology begins in 1934. Derived institutional is 1854 by the consolidation rule, while the first checked title naming Boolean algebras is Sheffer 1913. Peirce’s 1880 “algebra of logic” title is related terminology, not the name Boolean algebra. First monograph titled Boolean algebras: Sikorski 1960 (A, Zbl 0087.02503), not a milestone here.

Catalogue ID MB87/WB19

First statement 1956 · grade BFirst application 1958 · grade BNaming / consolidation 1962 · grade B

Search aliases Chomsky hierarchy · formal grammars · generative grammar · phrase-structure grammars · context-free languages · regular languages · automata theory · theory of formal languages

  1. 1956
    PrecursorGrammar models and automatamedium confidence

    Kleene, Representation of events in nerve nets and finite automata

    Independent automata-side work: regular events and finite automata.

    S. C. Kleene, Automata Studies (1956)

    1 linked source
    • CrossrefAutomata Studies chapter

    A (precursor) and B (independent). Same year as Chomsky 1956; included as precursor of the automata side.

  2. 1956
    First statementGrammar models and automatahigh confidence

    Chomsky, Three models for the description of language

    Compares finite-state, phrase-structure and transformational models of language.

    N. Chomsky, IRE Trans. Inf. Theory 2 (1956) 113-124

    1 linked source
    • Crossref / zbMATH 3251419IRE Transactions

    A, B and D. B notes the full hierarchy with machine classes is 1959. Publication year, not any talk, governs (D).

  3. 1958
    First applicationGrammar models and automatamedium confidence

    Chomsky and Miller, Finite state languages

    Grammar classes matched with finite-state automata, the first use of automata to classify languages.

    N. Chomsky, G. A. Miller, Inform. and Control 1 (1958) 91-112

    1 linked source
    • Elsevier, Information and Control articleThe article appeared in Information and Control 1(2), May 1958, pp. 91–112.

    A (1958-1959). B and D put method in 1956, using the same Chomsky 1956 paper (finite-state models tested against language); rejected because that is the first statement itself. Chosen 1958.

  4. 1959
    Key developmentGrammar models and automatahigh confidence

    Chomsky, On certain formal properties of grammars

    The hierarchy of grammar types 0-3 linked to machine classes.

    N. Chomsky, Inform. and Control 2 (1959) 137-167

    1 linked source
    • CrossrefInformation and Control 2

    A and B. B uses this paper as the earliest indexed title pairing formal with grammars (naming candidate, institutional 1959, low).

  5. 1959
    Key developmentGrammar models and automatamedium confidence

    Rabin and Scott, Finite automata and their decision problems

    Founding paper on nondeterministic finite automata.

    M. O. Rabin, D. Scott, IBM J. Res. Dev. 3 (1959)

    1 linked source
    • CrossrefIBM J. Res. Dev. 3

    A only.

  6. 1962
    NamingTextbook consolidationlow confidence

    Earliest indexed title with 'formal languages' (Burks and Wright)

    Earliest zbMATH title containing formal languages.

    Burks and Wright, 1962 (zbMATH 0109.35301)

    1 linked source
    • zbMATH OpenTitle search py:1955-1961 0 hits; 1962 first

    A only; B found 1960 (Bar-Hillel and Shamir) for 'formal representations', which is not the term. Term use only.

  7. 1963
    Key developmentTextbook consolidationmedium confidence

    Chomsky and Schutzenberger, The algebraic theory of context-free languages

    Algebraic side of context-free languages.

    N. Chomsky, M.-P. Schutzenberger, Computer Programming and Formal Systems (1963)

    1 linked source
    • CrossrefChapter

    B only.

  8. 1966
    ConsolidationTextbook consolidationmedium confidence

    Ginsburg, The mathematical theory of context-free languages

    First monograph on a major sub-area; the first textbook with formal languages in the title follows in 1968-69 (Engeler 1968, Hopcroft and Ullman 1969).

    S. Ginsburg, McGraw-Hill (1966)

    2 linked sources
    • zbMATH Zbl 0184.28401Monograph
    • zbMATH 0196.01701Hopcroft and Ullman, Formal languages and their relation to automata (1969)

    A (Engeler 1968, Hopcroft-Ullman 1969) and B (Ginsburg 1966 and HU 1969). Ginsburg is a sub-area monograph; kept as the earliest consolidation.

Research notes and unresolved questions

The event bundles fields and rings: Dedekind 1871, Weber 1893, Steinitz 1910 and Noether 1921 mark distinct claims. The 1930 textbook is consolidation rather than origin.
